front.title: Agent Name Service v2 (ANS): A Domain-Anchored Identity Layer for Autonomous AI Agents

abstract.t:
Autonomous AI agents now invoke one another across organizational boundaries over protocols such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent2Agent (A2A). A relying party has no interoperable way to bind a discoverable agent endpoint to the holder of its domain (optionally verified as a legal entity), a specific software release, and an auditable issuance history. This document specifies the architecture of Agent Name Service version 2 (ANS v2), an identity layer, anchored in DNS domains, that binds an agent endpoint to its domain holder, its release, and its history. ANS v2 composes systems the Internet already runs (the DNS with DNSSEC; the Web PKI, with DANE where operators publish it; and an append-only transparency log) and introduces no new root of trust.
Every ANS v2 agent carries a versioned name rooted in a DNS domain that the registrant controls. When a registrant registers an agent, the Registration Authority (RA) checks the registrant's control of that domain, can issue an Identity Certificate that binds the versioned name to the agent's key, and submits a signed registration record to a Merkle-tree transparency log. Under the current specifications, a new version is a new registration and a new log entry, so a verifier can pin an agent to a specific release. Any third party can detect a rewritten log by computing, from the log's public tiles, a consistency proof between two of its signed checkpoints.
For discovery, ANS v2 adopts the SVCB records and SvcParams of DNS for AI Discovery (DNS-AID) as its default format, and keeps an older TXT-based format only as an opt-in profile. Beyond those discovery records, ANS v2 specifies one DNS record, an "_ans-badge" TXT record that points to the agent's transparency-log entry; the log seals the fingerprint of the agent server's certificate, and operators can add DANE records. With these records, a verifier resolves an agent, authenticates its TLS endpoint, and confirms that the presented name, version, and key match a logged registration.
This document also states a threat model covering agent impersonation, DNS spoofing, CA and Registration Authority compromise, version rollback, agent card tampering, and log rewriting, and names what each ANS check does and does not prevent. The reference registry, transparency log, verifier, JSON Schemas, SDKs, and CLI are open source.
